clues.title: Architecture: Bali vibes
text: Architecture in Bali is unique because it was influenced by old Balinese culture and Hinduism. The most important thing to look for crown-like roof pinnacles, found everywhere in Bali. Guardian statues and slit-drum towers are common too. Andesite, a dark, volcanic rock, is a common building material in Bali. You can often see gates, walls, and other intricately carved ornaments built from this material.

text: Sumatran pines (Pinus merkusii) in Indonesia can be found in a few pockets across the country, notable areas include North Sumatra and Java. They can be recognised by having long needles for leaves, but be careful not to confuse them with she-oak, which has even longer leaves.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Vegetation - Coastal She-Oak
text: Coastal she-oak (Casuarina equisetifolia) can be found along the coast throughout much of the country, but particularly in Sumatra, Kalimantan and Java. Their leaves resemble the needles of pine trees, but are noticeably longer. Another species of she-oak can be found in mountainous regions throughout the country.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Vegetation - Palmyra
text: Palmyra palms (Borassus flabellifer) can be recognised by their fan-shaped leaves and dense round crowns. Compared to footstool palm, the crown is more dense, the leaves are heavier and the palm itself is usually shorter. It is found in dry parts of the country, namely the Nusas and South Sulawesi.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Vegetation - Footstool Palm
text: Footstool palm (Saribus rotundifolius) has fan-shaped leaves similar to those of Palmyra palm; however the crown is more open, the leaves are thinner and the palm itself is usually taller. It can be found most notably in Sulawesi and more rarely in other parts of the country.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Vegetation - Gebang Palm
text: Gebang palm (Corypha utan) can at first glance look similar to both Palmyra and footstool palm due to its fan-shaped leaves, however the leaves are noticeably larger, stiffer and more upright in contrast to the round crown shape of both Palmyra and footstool palm. Unlike most palms, the gebang palm will only flower once at the end of its life in a dramatic gesture where the leaves wither away and it shoots one large inflorescence into the heavens before it dies. It is found mainly in the east of the country, namely Sulawesi and the Nusas.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Agriculture - Cassava
text: Cassava (Manihot esculenta) can be recognised by its small, hand-shaped leaves. It can be found both in plantations as well as semi-wild in residential areas. It is most commonly seen in Lampung and Java with Lampung being the main hot spot.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Vegetation - Milkweed
text: Giant milkweed (Calotropis gigantea) is a small shrub with thick round leaves and pale flowers. It can be found in dry regions of Indonesia, namely the Nusas and parts of Java and Sulawesi.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Vegetation - White Leadtree
text: White leadtree (Leucaena leucocephala) can be recognised by its delicate featherlike (bipinnate) leaves. Fruits are often also visible in the form of legume pods. It can be found mainly in the Nusas as well as a few other dry areas of the country.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: Infrastructure - Indented Pole
text: Poles with an indent on both sides are found in West Java, Jakarta, and Banten.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Architecture - Malay Canopies
text: In the regions of Sumatra and Kalimantan that lie opposite Malaysia, many buildings have metal canopies with curved ends. These canopies are often blue or red.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Dragon Snake
text: In **Wajo Regency** you can also sometimes find **gable ornaments** in the shape of a **snake-like dragon with a raised head**.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Breaking Wave
text: This roof ornament with an **upward curling shape**, resembling a breaking wave, is exclusive to **South Sulawesi**, and specifically to **Wajo Regency**.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Dayak Horns
text: Recognisable by their **curved shape** and particularly **elaborate style**, these **gable horns** are mostly found in **North Kalimantan** and **East Kalimantan**, which have the largest Dayak populations.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Fighting Roosters
text: On **Selayar Island** you can find **gable horns** consisting of **crossed rooster heads**, sometimes also with **little figures of people** alongside.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Jambi Hooks
text: In **Jambi**, you can find **gable horns** consisting of **two hooks with downward-pointing ends**.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Crossed Bars
text: **Crossed roof ornaments** all along the **ridge of the roof** are found on **Nias Island**.

Please note that crossed bars can also be found elsewhere—for example, in Kalimantan on the so-called " Bubungan Tinggi " chief's house. This example involves the "rabbit ear" variant appearing multiple times on the same roof.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vertical Finial
text: Vertical finials are largely limited to **West Sulawesi**. They come in a **rounded** and a **flat** version.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: X
text: **X-shaped horns** share a similar distribution as winged gable horns, but can also sometimes be found in **Jambi** and on the **Riau Islands**.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Wings
text: The **‘winged’ gable horn** can be distinguished by its **serrated lower edge**. It is most common in **South Sulawesi** but can be found on much of the rest of Sulawesi and also in eastern Kalimantan.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Rabbit Ears
text: These **elongated and ornate ‘rabbit ear’ gable horns** are found in **South Kalimantan**.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Trident
text: These **ornate foliate trident-shaped gable horns** are found in **South Kalimantan**.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Floral Antlers
text: These **gable horns with rich floral patterns that resemble antlers** are found mostly in **Riau** and on the **Riau Islands**. These gable horns will often be seen accompanied by **similar floral decorations** on the gable itself.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Buffalo Horns
text: **Buffalo horn roof ornaments** have a similar distribution to ‘winged’ gable horns but are notably more common in **South East Sulawesi** and **West Sulawesi**.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Spear
text: On **Batam** and **Bintan** you will often see **simple, modern spear-shaped roof ornaments**, usually **painted gold or yellow**, or more rarely white. As with the Riau gable horns, they often accompany **floral gable decorations**.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Dagger
text: On **Rote Island** you can find this roof ornament, which resembles a **dagger amidst two upward-curving horns**.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Gable Ornaments
text: This **roof ornament** is characterised by its intricate foliate design and its **composition of three parts**: one vertical and two along the sides of the roof. It is present in **West Sulawesi**, as well as **South Kalimantan**.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
